_comment: Per-ASPSP SEPA Instant receiving limits, scoped to Berlin Group NextGenPSD2
participants — the framework this application already speaks.
Since the EPC removed the scheme-level ceiling, the maximum on an instant transfer is
each institution's own policy rather than a rule, so it has to be data. This file is
that data. It is read once at start-up and is immutable thereafter: to change a limit,
edit the entry and restart. There is deliberately no API for changing one at runtime,
so routing behaviour cannot move without a commit to review.
'maximum' absent means the bank has declared no ceiling — not that it accepts nothing.
Only institutions reachable on SEPA Instant need an entry; a bank that is not on the
scheme is handled by ReachabilityDirectory and never gets this far.
These are illustrative values for a sandbox. A production deployment takes them from
the EPC routing and reachability directory and each ASPSP's published API terms.

aspsps.name: Deutsche Bank
aspsps.note: Large participant; the old scheme ceiling retained as its own policy.

aspsps.name: Revolut
aspsps.note: Smaller institution, tighter per-transaction ceiling for liquidity reasons.

aspsps.name: BNP Paribas
aspsps.note: No ceiling declared, so only the sending institution's limit applies.
